$comment: Mach-O relocatable object (.o, MH_OBJECT) for x86_64 macOS / Darwin. Third shipped object-format JSON (plan 14 LK3, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/macho.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. mach_header_64 + section_64 + nlist_64 + relocation_info field values follow Apple's OS X ABI Mach-O File Format Reference + `<mach-o/loader.h>` / `<mach-o/nlist.h>` / `<mach-o/x86_64/reloc.h>`.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this artifact form has NO image header field for a stack size (a relocatable object / static archive is an INPUT to a later link, not a loadable program), so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request against it is REFUSED with an actionable remedy -- request the reserve on the build that produces the final EXECUTABLE image -- rather than silently dropped.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c-subset long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c-subset/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: macOS/Darwin (Apple x86_64 + arm64) uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation. Apple's enumerated arm64 ABI divergences from generic AAPCS64 are char/wchar_t signedness, long double=double, va_list, the red zone, the stack argument area, and empty-struct handling — NOT bit-field packing — so Mach-O shares gnu_packed. Byte-ABI-exact to clang, confirmed by the macOS CI cross-compile-compare leg (the only runtime witness for Apple).
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: macOS x86_64 `long double` = x87 80-bit, 16/16 (SysV). See macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec.

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity. cputype = CPU_TYPE_X86_64 (0x01000007 — CPU_ARCH_ABI64 bit OR'd with x86 ABI type 7). cpusubtype = CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_ALL (3). filetype = MH_OBJECT (1). flags = 0 — MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS (0x2000) is intentionally NOT set: the cycle-1 walker emits one flat `__text` blob with no N_ALT_ENTRY subsection markers, so advertising the flag would lie to ld64 about function-granular dead-strip safety (silent-failure-hunter HIGH-1 convergence). The flag will return when the substrate emits per-function subsections — anchored at plan 14 §3.1 D-LK3-2.

sections.$comment: Executable code. Mach-O two-level naming: section `__text` inside segment `__TEXT`. section_64.flags = S_REGULAR (0x0) | S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS (0x80000000) | S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (0x00000400) = 0x80000400. addrAlign in log2 form: 4 = 16 bytes. PE's substrate `type` field repurposed for Mach-O section_64.flags.
sections.name: __text

relocations.$comment: 32-bit PC-relative call/jmp. r_type = X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH (2), r_pcrel = 1, r_length = 2 (4 bytes). Mach-O `relocation_info.r_info` packs bits 28..31=r_type, 27=r_extern, 25..26=r_length, 24=r_pcrel, 0..23=r_symbolnum. The walker emits the static portion of r_info from this nativeId (type+length+pcrel = 0x25000000) and ORs in r_extern + r_symbolnum at emit time. `kind` = 1 matches x86_64.target.json's `rel32`. Mach-O has no Rela addend column — addends live in the patch bytes (the assembler writes 0; the linker computes target_va - (rip_after) - 0 since BRANCH is rip-relative).
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH

relocations.$comment: Absolute 64-bit. r_type = X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (0), r_pcrel = 0, r_length = 3 (8 bytes). nativeId = (0<<28)|(3<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x06000000. `kind` = 2 matches x86_64.target.json's `abs64`.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_8

relocations.$comment: Absolute 32-bit. r_type = X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (0), r_pcrel = 0, r_length = 2 (4 bytes). nativeId = (0<<28)|(2<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x04000000. `kind` = 3 matches x86_64.target.json's `abs32`.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_4
